blocks.text: SolMate findings: where Earth comes closest to NASA's Moon base regions and Mars sites

SolMate scored every land cell on Earth, about 1.9 million of them at 0.1°, against 11 NASA targets: the nine Artemis III candidate base regions near the lunar south pole, Jezero Crater and Arcadia Planitia. Each place gets a SolMate Analog Index (SAI, 0–100) built from seven characteristics measured with 41 NASA data layers, a statement of where the analogy breaks down, and what the place could be used for.

The method was checked against sites NASA has already used as analogs, with a test written down before the results: for Jezero, documented Mars analog sites outscore controls with an AUC of 0.84 (95% CI 0.69–0.96); the Moon regions reach a median of 0.75, and Arcadia Planitia 0.58, which is reported as a weak result.
Interactive version: https://solmate-analog.web.app/findings · Explorer: https://solmate-analog.web.app/explorer · Method: https://solmate-analog.web.app/method
Headline findings

items: High, cold, barren plateaus are Earth's closest match to both worlds. Of the top five places for each of the 11 targets (55 in all), 35 lie on the Tibetan Plateau and 16 in the Puna de Atacama, roughly 3,500–5,000 m high (judged from NASA POWER surface pressure).

52 of those 55 are more than 300 km from all 31 known analog sites (NASA field sites, the Atacama, Antarctica, Iceland, Hawaiʻi, Devon Island and others): leads nobody has tested, listed for expert and field review.

No place matches everything. Nowhere on Earth is as cold, as dry or as airless as the lunar south pole or Mars; those characteristics are ranked toward the target, and the gap is stated with every result.
Different places lead on different characteristics: the best terrain match is often not the best thermal or mineral match, which is why every result shows all seven dimensions.

blocks.text: Best places for every target
SAI with equal weights, with terrain measured at 100 m from NASA ASTER GDEM where available. A novel lead is more than 300 km from every known analog site.
Case study: Jezero Crater (Mars) and the Tibetan Plateau
The best novel lead for Jezero Crater is the cell at 37.05°N 86.75°E, 477 km from the nearest known analog site, Qaidam Basin (Dalangtan). Its SAI is 85.0.

Where the analogy breaks down

items: Gravity is 0.38x Earth: Earth tests overload structures, wheels and people.
Surface pressure is 0.01x this place: no Earth site reproduces vacuum or the thin Martian air (heat transfer, dust lofting, boiling).
Surface radiation dose is 97.4x Earth: Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field shield every analog site.

blocks.text: What it could be used for

items: Landing-pad, regolith-handling and construction trials on flat barren ground.
Instrument and habitat thermal-cycling tests in large day-night temperature swings.
Ice prospecting, drilling and ISRU rehearsals in frozen ground.

How far to trust it

AUC is the chance that a site NASA has used as an analog outscores a control (farmland, forest, cities, ice); 0.5 is chance. The last column counts each 500 km cluster of sites once, a check added after mentor review and written down before it was run.

items: Jezero is the strongest result; the Moon targets have only 10 analog sites each, so their intervals are wide.
Arcadia Planitia is weak with equal weights and is reported rather than hidden.
Terrain-first Moon weights (Lunar ops) were tested after mentor review: they help the rugged massifs and hurt the plateaus, so equal weights stay the default.

blocks.text: Limits

items: Gravity, atmosphere, radiation and surface chemistry differ from Earth everywhere; they are stated, never scored.
A 0.1° cell averages about 11 km of ground; only terrain is refined at 100 m.
Novel leads are unreviewed: they need expert review and field data before anyone plans a test.
Validation labels reflect where agencies have worked, which includes logistics as well as science.

blocks.text: Data and reproducibility

All scored inputs are NASA data: MODIS (MYD11C3, MOD10CM, MCD43C3, MCD12C1), ASTER GED and GDEM v3, MERRA-2, NASA POWER and SRTMGL30 on Earth; LRO LOLA and Diviner on the Moon; MOLA, CTX and Mars 2020 results on Mars. Sources, licences and checksums: https://solmate-analog.web.app/provenance. Code: https://github.com/Tanbin-CS/solmate (results version 50a1ccf90b2a).
